title: ramfs snapshots read length before serializing with resize
mechanism: RamInode::read_at reads the file size and computes read_len before taking the page-cache lock, then returns the saved read_len after Vmo::read silently clamps the copy to the current VMO capacity. A concurrent ftruncate or extending write in that gap makes the returned count differ from the bytes delivered, and InodeHandle::read advances the shared offset by the stale count.
contract: read(2)/pread(2): the returned count equals the bytes stored in the buffer, and read advances the offset by exactly that count, even when racing truncate or an extending write.
observed: pread64 of a 4096-byte ramfs file racing ftruncate(fd, 0) returned 4096 while delivering 0 bytes, and read(2) advanced the shared offset by 4096 with 0 or 8192 bytes delivered.
fix_refs: /home/chin39/Documents/asterinas-dev branch fix/ramfs-read-past-eof: 16e1bcaa6 (Serialize ramfs reads with resizing), d007cbb62 (fs/read_truncate_race test)

repro.how_to_run: Boot an Asterinas kernel with -smp 2 and an initramfs whose /init is test_bugMC-1_init.c and whose /test_mc1 is test_bugMC-1_ramfs_saved_count.c. MC1_RESULT BUG_TRIGGERED means the bug fired. For a fix, apply read_truncate_race-regression.patch and run the fs regression suite with SMP=4.
